findings.originalDescription: Anyone can self-register an email they don't own; when that person is later invited (staff or customer team), acceptance attaches the role to the attacker's account and discards the invitee's password
findings.originalStatus: FAIL — reproduced locally (attacker reached /staff/projects as developer)
findings.requiredFix: On accept: if the existing account is unverified, reset credentials, factors and sessions and quarantine its self-created org; otherwise require sign-in as that verified user. Refuse staff invites to existing customer accounts
findings.acceptanceTest: Register X unverified → invite X → accept with P2: P1 fails, P2 works, old sessions invalid; same for customer-team invite
findings.rootCause: acceptInvitation attached the invited role to any existing users row with the invited email, without proving the token holder owned that account; registration does not prove email ownership.
findings.evidence: 6 adversarial tests in tests/invitation-security.test.ts pass (staff takeover blocked, attacker MFA/sessions/tokens revoked, verified account requires sign-in, customer-team parity, staff→verified-customer refusal, concurrent single use); full suite 448/448; CI test check green on PR #26.
findings.notes: Originally PR #26 (claude/closeout-001-invitation-takeover); consolidated into PR #37.

findings.originalDescription: Anonymous attacker can lock any account, including the Owner, indefinitely: the lock slides with each failure and the per-email limit returns 429 even to the correct password; no challenge on /login. Staging Owner email is public, and the lock also breaks staging deploy verification
findings.originalStatus: FAIL — code and local PoC; no branch fixes it
findings.requiredFix: Progressive throttling per account and IP, known-device bypass, count failures only, never extend a lock, Turnstile on /login after N failures, Owner unlock and alert
findings.acceptanceTest: 50 wrong passwords from 5 IPs → Owner on known device still reaches /mfa; lock never extends
findings.rootCause: A per-email lock slid forward on each failure and returned 429 even for the right password, so anyone could lock any account.
findings.evidence: Progressive throttling: per IP, per IP+address and per remembered browser; Turnstile challenge for unknown browsers after 5 failures; no lock is ever set (migration 0046 releases existing locks). Test: 50 wrong passwords from 5 IPs cannot keep the Owner out of the remembered browser. 476/476.
findings.notes: Founder default applied: progressive throttling, no indefinite lockout. Originally PR #29 (claude/closeout-003-login-throttling); consolidated into PR #37.

findings.originalDescription: Cookie lacks \_\_Host- prefix; token not rotated when MFA completes
findings.rootCause: Session and CSRF cookies had no __Host- prefix and the session token was not rotated after MFA.
findings.evidence: __Host-cm_session / __Host-cm_csrf over HTTPS (both names read during rollout), rotateSessionToken after completeMfa and confirmTotpEnrollment. 478/478.

findings.originalDescription: Signed evidence, scheduler and runner endpoints accept replays within 10 minutes
findings.rootCause: Signed machine requests were accepted again within their 10-minute validity.
findings.evidence: Runner bodies carry a fresh _nonce per attempt; the control plane refuses a reused nonce (409); RUNNER_REQUIRE_NONCE=yes refuses bodies without one. Evidence ingest is idempotent by run id; the scheduler is rate limited. Runner 92/92.
findings.notes: Set RUNNER_REQUIRE_NONCE=yes once every runner is updated. Originally PR #30 (claude/closeout-hardening); consolidated into PR #37.

findings.originalDescription: Public /api/readiness/health lists feed names and reasons; anyone can self-register customer accounts on staging
findings.rootCause: Public health shows feed names and sanitized failure reasons; staging allows self-registration.
findings.evidence: Kept by design: external monitors and the staging journeys need named feeds; only failing infrastructure feeds expose a short sanitized reason ('[INFRA-006] failing infrastructure feeds expose a short sanitized public reason; nothing else does'); staging self-registration is required by the staging journeys and is safe after #26 (invitation takeover fixed) and #35 (verified email before checkout).
findings.notes: Revisit if the Founder wants staging registration restricted.

findings.originalDescription: Lockouts, MFA failures and recovery-code use alert nobody beyond the account holder

findings.notes: login_challenge_started is emitted by the login-throttling PR #29; the alert already handles it. Originally PR #36 (claude/closeout-ops); consolidated into PR #37.

supplemental.originalDescription: Staging journey 4 asserted 'Online payment is not configured yet.', so adding a Stripe test key to staging would fail every deploy; journeys 5–7 and 24 were permanently blocked even once Stripe test mode exists.

supplemental.rootCause: The journeys were written when staging could not have Stripe; full commerce (decision A) makes Stripe test mode on staging the expected state.
supplemental.externalRequirements: Runs only against deployed staging with a Stripe test key; first real run happens after the Founder adds the key.
supplemental.evidence: Journey 4 accepts either state; payOnStripeCheckout refuses non-cs_test_ sessions; certification summary published per deploy. tsc clean; local e2e 37/0 (staging journeys skip without staging).
